passage:
Tanvir stared at his maths paper. Thirty-one. In the corridor he slid down against the wall. "It's over. Nothing's going to change. I'm just bad at this."
Darshan sat down beside him. "It's one paper."
"It doesn't matter."
Darshan didn't argue. After a bit he asked, "Which questions lost you the marks?"
"The last three."
"Then we start with those. I'm free after school on Thursday." He glanced at Tanvir. "And show your mum tonight. Then you're not carrying this alone."
Tanvir was silent for a long time. He picked up the paper and smoothed it against his knee. "Okay," he said. "Three questions."

qa.q: What mark did Tanvir get on the maths paper?
What was Tanvir feeling as he slid down the corridor wall?
qa.a: Tanvir felt hopeless and discouraged, saying nothing would change and that he was just bad at maths.

qa.q: What did Darshan offer that helped widen Tanvir's view?
qa.a: Darshan asked which questions lost the marks and offered to work on those on Thursday. He also suggested showing Tanvir's mum that night so Tanvir would not carry it alone.

qa.q: How might Darshan have felt seeing Tanvir slide down the wall?
qa.a: Darshan was probably worried and wanted to help, so Darshan stayed calm, sat beside Tanvir and did not argue with the hopeless words.

grounding: A teenager who failed an exam concludes everything is ruined, and a friend offers a concrete next step and a trusted adult.

passage:
"It's ruined, Papa. Everything." Deepika dropped her bag on the sofa. "I failed the science test. I won't get into anything now."
Her father, Madhav, sat beside her. "Show me."
"There's nothing to show."
"Show me anyway."
She pulled out the paper. Thirty-four. "See?"
"Which section lost the marks?"
"The diagrams. I never learned them."
"So not everything. One section." He took a pencil and wrote DIAGRAMS at the top of the page. "Saturday, one hour, only diagrams. And Monday you ask Miss Nair what she suggests for the next test."
"You think it'll change?"
"I think diagrams can be learned. Come, tea first."
She leaned into his shoulder, sighed, and followed him to the kitchen.

qa.q: What section lost Deepika the marks?
qa.a: The diagrams lost her the marks.

qa.q: What was Deepika feeling when she dropped her bag and said it was ruined?
qa.a: Deepika felt hopeless and scared about her future, believing one failed test meant she would not get into anything.

qa.q: What did Madhav do that made the problem smaller?
qa.a: Madhav asked which section lost the marks and pointed out it was one section. He then set a small plan, one hour of diagrams on Saturday and a question to Miss Nair on Monday.

qa.q: How might Madhav have felt hearing Deepika say everything was ruined?
qa.a: Madhav was probably concerned and wanted to steady her, which is why he asked to see the paper and stayed calm and practical.

grounding: A teenager who failed a test concludes everything is ruined; a parent offers a concrete next step that widens her view.
